editorial.description_en: Moss seen through mist: a light grey that turns green only when you look for it. Its hue sits on the warm-cool bisector, so the corpus records it as neutral rather than picking a side.
editorial.description_ja: 霧の中の苔のような、緑がかったうすい灰色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.786, C 0.013, h 148.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 霧 (kiri, mist) + 苔 (koke, moss), rendaku to -goke. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Mist Moss" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 霧苔. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — tani-giri at ΔE00 5.5, sawa-ishi at ΔE00 7.7, kumori-garasu at ΔE00 7.9. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.013 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
